Definition: to tan (by sunburning); figuratively (as if by a piercing ray) to scan
BiblicalUsage: To look on, in this word, is to be seen by the sun and by men. Job says the eye which saw the wicked shall see him no more, and the vulture's eye has not seen the hidden path, but the Song gives the human verse: look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me. The sun's look darkened her, and her brothers' anger set her to keep vineyards.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being looked on can wound and can love, for the sun looked on her and darkened her, and I hold that the Lord's look is different: He sees and He keeps.
